assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational empirical account of how technology, trade exposure and task content reshape labour demand and wage inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor’s task framework and the Autor-Dorn-Hanson empirical program form a coherent, highly influential contribution; the listed trio captures its central credit.
assessment.maturity: The findings and associated methods have shaped labour economics and policy discussion for many years.
uncertainties: The separate causal contributions of automation, trade and broader local adjustment remain difficult to disentangle.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population administrative data have made intergenerational mobility measurable at an unprecedented scale and transformed research on opportunity and place.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are central architects of the linked-data mobility research program, though its production is substantially collaborative.
assessment.maturity: The empirical framework is widely used and its core descriptive facts have persisted across a large body of work.
uncertainties: The interpretation of place effects and the policy mechanisms behind mobility estimates remains contested.
Credit is difficult to compress because of the program's extensive collaboration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The modern analysis of monopsony has changed how economists understand wage setting, employer power and labour-market policy.
assessment.attribution: Manning provided the especially unifying theoretical and empirical synthesis; other listed researchers made major but less singularly defining contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework is long established and has generated a large subsequent empirical literature.
uncertainties: The magnitude and institutional sources of employer power vary considerably across labour markets.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on early-life health, shocks and skill formation has established childhood conditions as central determinants of later economic outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Currie and Almond supplied influential quasi-experimental evidence, while Cunha made core contributions to dynamic skill-formation analysis.
assessment.maturity: The insight is supported by a broad, mature body of evidence across settings.
uncertainties: Long-run causal estimates can be context-dependent, and biological, family and institutional mechanisms remain hard to separate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Correspondence and audit studies made discrimination directly testable in realistic labour-market settings and set an influential empirical standard.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan are the clearest central credit for the landmark modern correspondence-study contribution.
assessment.maturity: The design has been extensively replicated, adapted and integrated into research and policy evaluation.
uncertainties: Measured callback discrimination is not identical to discrimination at hiring, pay or promotion stages.
External validity depends on occupation, locality and application design.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The combination of theory and credible measurement of selection in insurance markets has materially improved the design and evaluation of insurance policy.
assessment.attribution: Finkelstein, Einav and Salanie represent complementary central contributions to empirical and theoretical analysis of selection.
assessment.maturity: The program has been influential for decades and applies well beyond health insurance.
uncertainties: Welfare conclusions depend on market-specific assumptions about risk, information, pricing and consumer behaviour.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Work on teacher quality, school incentives and educational production has recast education policy around measurable effectiveness and causal evidence.
assessment.attribution: Kane, Hanushek and Hoxby are prominent contributors, but the discovery label aggregates several related research programs and makes a narrow allocation difficult.
assessment.maturity: Teacher-effectiveness measurement and school-accountability research have had sustained scholarly and policy impact.
uncertainties: Accountability and value-added estimates are sensitive to design choices and institutional context.
The candidate grouping may be too heterogeneous for a single prize attribution.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural analysis of labour supply, taxation and household intertemporal choices supplied durable tools for evaluating tax and transfer policy.
assessment.attribution: Blundell, Meghir and MaCurdy made central contributions to the modelling and empirical implementation of this program.
assessment.maturity: These methods are well established and remain influential in public and labour economics.
uncertainties: Structural policy conclusions depend on behavioural assumptions, measurement and extrapolation beyond observed reforms.
